messages.text: How do changes in radar technology affect the measurement capability required from Signaling / Non-signaling Tester?

### Short answer
【推論】Radar-related evolution toward ISAC / joint communication-radar sensing and higher-bandwidth sensing means a signaling / non-signaling tester must go beyond ordinary communications RF/protocol checks when radar behavior is part of the DUT: it must cover the relevant frequency/bandwidth, waveform/spectrum coexistence, and possibly radar-specific echo, distance, and Doppler behavior; otherwise a dedicated radar echo generator is needed.[24][92][6][18][81][89]
### Supported facts
The CMX500 signaling scope in the passages is communications-focused: LTE, 5G, and Wi‑Fi UE signaling over 400 MHz to 8 GHz, with RF measurements such as Power, Frequency, Spectrum, EVM, PER/BLER, and MIMO, plus application-layer and protocol tests [6].
The CMX500 non-signaling GPRF use case can generate ARB, CW, dual tone, or replay `.wv` waveforms for R&D waveform replay / creation and standalone TX measurement workflows [25][27].
ISAC integrates sensing capability into communications networks, and its challenges include high bandwidth, radar equation, power density, spectrum coexistence, and waveform design [24].
MFSS may integrate joint waveforms such as communications plus radar sensing, or communications methods that provide timing information [92].
Automotive radar echo generation in the passages is a different measurement role: the AREG800A provides dynamic artificial object generation, with hybrid or digital echo generation for FMCW radar and maximum generated distance up to 3000 m [18].
Radar-specific capability can include artificial-object Doppler/velocity behavior: AREG800A supports individual Doppler frequency shift per artificial object, velocity setting range of ±500 km/h, and velocity accuracy < 0.05 km/h under the stated conditions [81].
Radar-specific bandwidth and frequency needs can be much higher than the cited CMX500 UAV signaling range: AREG800A source data lists base-unit instantaneous IF bandwidth options of 1 GHz, 2 GHz, or 5 GHz, and radar RF bands including 76 GHz to 81 GHz for several 81 GHz frontends / QAT100 [89].
### Practical impact
【推論】If the radar change is only “radar-like coexistence with communications,” the tester need mainly expands toward spectrum, waveform, interference/coexistence, and possibly non-signaling waveform replay capabilities.[24][25][27]
【推論】If the radar change requires validating actual radar sensing behavior, a normal signaling tester’s LTE/5G/Wi‑Fi RF/protocol scope is insufficient by itself, because the cited radar validation needs include generated distance, artificial objects, Doppler/velocity, and 76 GHz to 81 GHz radar coverage.[6][18][81][89]

### Short answer
【推論】Radar-related evolution toward ISAC / joint communication-radar sensing and higher-bandwidth sensing means a signaling / non-signaling tester must go beyond ordinary communications RF/protocol checks when radar behavior is part of the DUT: it must cover the relevant frequency/bandwidth, waveform/spectrum coexistence, and possibly radar-specific echo, distance, and Doppler behavior; otherwise a dedicated radar echo generator is needed.[24][92][6][18][81][89]
### Supported facts
The CMX500 signaling scope in the passages is communications-focused: LTE, 5G, and Wi‑Fi UE signaling over 400 MHz to 8 GHz, with RF measurements such as Power, Frequency, Spectrum, EVM, PER/BLER, and MIMO, plus application-layer and protocol tests [6].
The CMX500 non-signaling GPRF use case can generate ARB, CW, dual tone, or replay `.wv` waveforms for R&D waveform replay / creation and standalone TX measurement workflows [25][27].
ISAC integrates sensing capability into communications networks, and its challenges include high bandwidth, radar equation, power density, spectrum coexistence, and waveform design [24].
MFSS may integrate joint waveforms such as communications plus radar sensing, or communications methods that provide timing information [92].
Automotive radar echo generation in the passages is a different measurement role: the AREG800A provides dynamic artificial object generation, with hybrid or digital echo generation for FMCW radar and maximum generated distance up to 3000 m [18].
Radar-specific capability can include artificial-object Doppler/velocity behavior: AREG800A supports individual Doppler frequency shift per artificial object, velocity setting range of ±500 km/h, and velocity accuracy < 0.05 km/h under the stated conditions [81].
Radar-specific bandwidth and frequency needs can be much higher than the cited CMX500 UAV signaling range: AREG800A source data lists base-unit instantaneous IF bandwidth options of 1 GHz, 2 GHz, or 5 GHz, and radar RF bands including 76 GHz to 81 GHz for several 81 GHz frontends / QAT100 [89].
### Practical impact
【推論】If the radar change is only “radar-like coexistence with communications,” the tester need mainly expands toward spectrum, waveform, interference/coexistence, and possibly non-signaling waveform replay capabilities.[24][25][27]
【推論】If the radar change requires validating actual radar sensing behavior, a normal signaling tester’s LTE/5G/Wi‑Fi RF/protocol scope is insufficient by itself, because the cited radar validation needs include generated distance, artificial objects, Doppler/velocity, and 76 GHz to 81 GHz radar coverage.[6][18][81][89]
